Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, um Jordan, Priya, good to see you all. quick agenda — renewal cadence, eu capacity uplift, and sovereignty options. Rafael's gonna cover the benchmark ask.
[00:18] Jordan Blake: hey maya, yeah thanks. we've been ramping chat volumes, the spike last week made the P95 go funky so we want to understand what a small dedicated bump would look like. Also we need the data residency bit — legal's pressing for that.
[00:36] Priya Nair: and just to add, our compliance lead flagged KMS integration for keys. we need optional HSM, ideally bring-your-own-key, and audit logs retained 1 year. is that supported?
[00:50] Rafael Ortiz: short answer yes — Redwood supports BYOK via KMS integrations, HSM in private deployments. audit logs are available in the console with configurable retention. i'll send the docs but as a caveat different retention tiers are an add-on.
[01:08] Samir Desai: are there any throughput guarantees for a dedicated pool? our ops team wants predictable token per second numbers not just a vague SLA.
[01:22] Leah Tran: we can put commitments in the dedicated contract — committed TPS/throughput and burst lanes. SLA language varies by contract level. we can share a sizing matrix.
[01:34] Jordan Blake: ok good. can we do a short benchmark? like 72 hours with our traffic shape and see P50/P95 and cost deltas for hosted vs dedicated?
[01:46] Rafael Ortiz: yes that's doable. we'll need a sample of prompt distribution and typical sequence lengths — Priya if you can share that we can mirror the workload. i'll run two runs: hosted profile with caching and a dedicated GPU pool without prefix cache to see worst-case.
[02:05] Priya Nair: i can share the request histogram, it's mostly short chat turns but with occasional long context pushes to ~2k tokens.
[02:15] Maya Chen: quick note, for the EU uplift we usually recommend starting with a small reserved capacity block and then evaluate autoscaling. it reduces unit cost relative to pure burst.
[02:28] Jordan Blake: cost is big for us — TitanServe gave us a figure that was lower on raw price but their latency under similar patterns was worse, so tradeoffs. do you have a clear per-token cost delta?
[02:45] Maya Chen: i'll share the worksheet. but important: we optimize for cost with batching and KV/prefix caching — so if your workload benefits from cache (repeated prompts, assistant persona), the hosted per-token effective cost drops a lot. Rafael can show expected uplift numbers after the benchmark.
[03:05] Rafael Ortiz: also — small transcription note: k v cache sometimes in our docs shows up as KV cache, but in some transcriptions might read oddly.
[03:15] Ava Hopkins: procurement — timeline question: our renewal window is early April. we need contractual terms nailed by mid-March to route through finance. is that feasible?
[03:27] Maya Chen: yes, mid-March is doable. we should aim to share pricing options and a sample contract by next week.
[03:33] Jordan Blake: on sovereignty, can Redwood run the control plane in a customer VPC, or is it always redwood managed? we want to avoid sending metadata outside EU.
[03:45] Rafael Ortiz: there are two paths: Private deployment where the control plane runs in your VPC (or on-prem package), or Hosted with regional residency controls — but metadata could still flow to Redwood control plane depending on configuration. For strict sovereignty, the private control-plane package is the answer. note that private has longer lead times and a different support model.
[04:10] Priya Nair: technical-deep dive — latency numbers: we want <120ms P95 for single-turn, that's our SLO for EU customers. is that realistic with committed capacity?
[04:22] Rafael Ortiz: depends on model size and quantization. For mid-size models on A100-like HW with continuous batching, sub-120ms P95 is achievable for typical prompt lengths. With long 2k contexts it's harder. The benchmark will clarify.
[04:45] Jordan Blake: what about on-prem? we have an air-gapped pilot next quarter, is that an option?
[04:53] Maya Chen: yes, we offer an on-prem package — customers have used it for regulated pilots. again longer procurement and security review. we can coordinate the security deep-dive to walk those steps.
[05:07] Priya Nair: in a private control plane, does Redwood still have access to logs for support? we need to be sure about access and auditability.
[05:18] Rafael Ortiz: access can be restricted — support can be given via collected bundles or read-only APIs if you want. we can document the exact support path for private installs.
[05:30] Samir Desai: small thing — do you offer SSO / SAML with SCIM and RBAC fine-grained roles?
[05:38] Leah Tran: yes, SSO/SAML plus SCIM provisioning and role-based access. enterprise tier adds deeper session/role controls.
[05:45] Jordan Blake: curious competitor note — BigCloud AI said they could do EU-only but their cache strategy was global so not great for us.
[05:55] Maya Chen: understood. Redwood's smart routing can keep traffic in-region and fallback rules if a region is busy.
[06:05] Priya Nair: okay so next steps, we'll share our traffic histogram and top 20 prompts, procurement timeline. Redwood will share pricing worksheet, benchmark plan, and security docs.
[06:18] Ava Hopkins: and we'll need the PO template.
[06:22] Maya Chen: got it — i'll include PO template. Rafael, you'll own the benchmark?
[06:26] Rafael Ortiz: yes i'll set up a 72-hour run — i'll need creds and a sample dataset, plus an endpoint to push metrics to.
[06:38] Jordan Blake: how about a canary — if the benchmark looks good can we spin up a small dedicated pool for a week in eu-central to validate in prod?
[06:49] Rafael Ortiz: that's a common approach. we can do a short pilot with traffic mirroring. Concerns: cost of dedicated week, but it's a good safety check.
[07:00] Priya Nair: mirror only 10% of traffic to start. If we see P95 within target then scale.
[07:07] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood to share pricing worksheet by 2026-03-02, Rafael to run benchmark by 2026-03-05, schedule compliance deep-dive week of 2026-03-08. Aventus to share histograms by 2026-02-27 and procurement timeline/PO by 2026-03-01.
[07:30] Jordan Blake: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:34] Leaky speaker / crosstalk - (unintelligible)
[07:40] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to the bench plan and docs.

End of transcript.
